title: Siegard ADR frontmatter
description: Frontmatter contract for an architecture decision record in docs/adr/. The prose format is documented in docs/adr/README.md; this file is the authority for the frontmatter. Supersession and amendment are structured here so a validator can decide them rather than a reader inferring them from prose. Version 2 adds `amends`, for an ADR that reverses part of another while leaving the rest in force; no ADR currently declares it. Adding that field to schemas/adr.v1.json in place would have made previously invalid instances valid, which .claude/rules/compatibility.md defines as a breaking change, so v1 is kept readable and every ADR was migrated in the same change.

id.description: Four-digit sequential id, never reused, matching the filename prefix. Must be a quoted string: YAML reads an unquoted 0010 as octal 8 and an unquoted 0008 as a string, so the unquoted form is neither safe nor type-stable.

title.description: The decision stated as an outcome.

status.description: Lifecycle vocabulary defined in docs/adr/README.md and shared with schemas/spec.v1.json and schemas/concept.v1.json. Only a maintainer, or a deterministic approval mechanism this repository defines, may change this value away from proposed.

contract_version.description: A consumer rejects an artifact it was not built to read rather than inferring version from shape. An ADR still declaring adr/1 is validated against schemas/adr.v1.json, so it is detectably outdated rather than silently non-conforming.

superseded_by.description: Id of the ADR that replaced this one. Required when status is superseded, and forbidden otherwise: a supersession relation that points nowhere, or points from a live decision, is a defect rather than history.

amends.description: Id of an ADR whose decision this one revises in part, leaving the rest of that decision in force. Distinct from superseded_by, which retires a decision whole. The amendment binds only while this ADR is accepted; on a proposed ADR it records intent. scripts/validate_adrs.py additionally requires the amended ADR's body to cite the amending id, because frontmatter a reader does not see cannot warn them that the decision they are reading has moved.

superseded_by.description: Stating a replacement is what makes a decision superseded. Expressed as a dependency rather than as a negated allOf branch so the failure names the offending field instead of dumping the document.
